message:
Plain words: the chassis stows inside the start box and then widens for stability. The side and top view folding chassis sketch (E24) shows fold arms tucked to 0.90 m long by 0.45 m wide by 0.45 m high against the 1.0 m by 0.5 m by 0.5 m limit, about the size of a suitcase with room to spare.

Plain words: wide grouser wheels float on loose simulant and pull far harder than digging needs. The Development and Field Testing of Moonraker: a Four-Wheel Rover in Minimal Design (E14) built 200 mm diameter wheels with 10 mm grousers and reported good travel to about 10 deg loose slope, so I use that wheel size for soft soil. Ground pressure is about 15.6 kPa from the ground pressure estimate (E25), softer than a person standing on one foot, and available traction is about 294 N against about 32.9 N cut load from the BP-1 shallow scraper cut force estimate (E9), a margin of 8.90 times from the tip-over and stopping check (E23).

Plain words: the raised rear pour will not tip the robot and it stops in a hand length. Stabilising moment about the rear axle is about 206 N m against about 44.1 N m overturning with 15.0 kg carried soil for a factor of 4.67, and stopping from 0.50 m per s takes about 62.5 mm in 0.25 s, from the tip-over and stopping check (E23), both small against a 60 kg machine. Not ready, because Power Structure and Integration Lead must still confirm the 60 kg mass sum and Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead must confirm slip correction for skid steering.
